It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Fudaten Shrine'''|布多天神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

It is the {{ill|Manuel de Barros|Q10324625|qid=Q10324625}} of {{ill|Fuda Goshuku|Q28690549|qid=Q28690549}} and is also called “Goshuku Tenjin”{{sfn|Tokyo Shrine Office}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
Originally {{ill|Sukunabikona|ca|Sukunabikona|fr|Sukunabikona|it|Sukuna-hikona|ja|スクナビコナ|ko|스쿠나비코나|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯕꯤꯀꯣꯅ|pl|Sukunabikona|pt|Sukunahikona|simple|Sukunabikona|sv|Suku-Na-Bikona|zh|少彥名|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunabikona-no-Kami}} was the deity, and at the time of relocation {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}} was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}.

Because the name Fudaten Shrine appears in the Engishiki, it is one of the shrines called “{{ill|Tenjinsha|Q11443279|qid=Q11443279}}” from before enshrining Sugawara no Michizane. There are various examples of shrines with Sukunabikona-no-Kami as main deity being called Tenjin-sha.

== Foundation ==
The founding date is unknown. Shrine tradition says it was founded about 1,940 years ago in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}. It is an ancient shikinaisha listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} (compiled in {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) under Tama District, Musashi Province{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki, Kami-Fuda-juku}}.

The original shrine stood in today’s Fuda 5-chōme. After major flooding of the {{ill|Tama River|Q1063006|qid=Q1063006}} in the {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544}} era, it moved to the current location in Bunmei 9 ({{ill|1477|Q6614|qid=Q6614}}) and merged Sugawara no Michizane{{sfn|Tokyo Shrine Office}}.

A “Taikō proclamation board” from April {{ill|1590|Q6764|qid=Q6764}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 18), issued by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}} during his Odawara campaign to reassure people, remains in shrine holdings.

The former shrine site now has “Kotenjin Park.” Excavation in Shōwa 55 found traces from about 10,000 years ago ({{ill|Paleolithic|Q40203|qid=Q40203}}), settlement traces from about 4,000-5,000 years ago ({{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}}), and tombs from about 1,500 years ago.

Villages of Fuda Goshuku (Fuda-Kojima-bun, Kami-Ishihara, Shimo-Ishihara, Kami-Fuda, Shimo-Fuda, and Kokuryō-juku) merged with Tobitagyū and Kamigakyū in 1889 (Meiji 22) to form {{ill|Chōfu|Q11631758|qid=Q11631758}}, making this shrine the general guardian shrine of Chōfu Town.

== Cultural properties ==
== Chōfu City designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural property
** Fudaten Shrine honden (with one ridge tag) (building) - designated December 25, 1998.
* Tangible folk cultural properties
** Fudaten Shrine komainu pair - designated November 12, 1969.
** Fudaten Shrine Taikō proclamation board - designated September 8, 1971.

== Antique market ==
An {{ill|antique market|Q11668600|qid=Q11668600}} is held on the second Sunday of every month, with around 20-30 stalls<ref name="tsugesanpo">[https://tsugesanpo.sakura.ne.jp/18.html Walking with Tsuge Yoshiharu (Chōfu edition) official site, 18. Fudaten Shrine]</ref>.

== Setting in works ==
== In works by Shigeru Mizuki ==
In {{ill|Shigeru Mizuki|Q669049|qid=Q669049}}’s ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hakaba Kitarō}}'' and ''{{ill|GeGeGe no Kitarō|Q1368693|qid=Q1368693}}'', Kitarō is set as living in the forest behind the honden. Mizuki, who lived in {{ill|Chōfu|Q210667|qid=Q210667}}, is said to have used the forest of Fudaten Shrine, connected to Taishōji cemetery, as inspiration. In season 6 of the TV anime, following the original work and set in Chōfu, there is a scene where Kitarō returns to the back of the precinct<ref name="anime">{{Cite web|和書|title=Visit locations of the anime "GeGeGe no Kitarō"! Pilgrimage map distribution starts in Chōfu, Tokyo|url=https://animetourism88.com/ja/news/1474|website=Anime Tourism Association - 88 Sacred Sites|accessdate=2019-02-14|language=ja}}</ref>.

The approach from {{ill|Old Kōshū Kaidō|Q11511097|qid=Q11511097}} is lined with shops as “Tenjin-dōri Shopping Street,” and as a revitalization project, statues of yōkai characters from ''GeGeGe no Kitarō'' are installed<ref name="anime" />.

== Other ==
*In Tsuge Yoshiharu’s ''{{ill|The Man Without Talent|Q3203779|qid=Q3203779}}'' series episode “Selling the Camera,” the temple-fair antique market is depicted. The last scene with Sukegawa and his child heading quietly toward the {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} after leaving Fudaten Shrine is memorable<ref name="tsugesanpo"></ref>.
*Used as a location in the 1997 TV drama ''{{ill|Aoi Tori|Q11661048|qid=Q11661048|lt=Aoi Tori}}'', depicted as a shrine in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}.
*Used as a location in the 2019 TV drama ''{{ill|Your Turn to Kill|Q61058243|qid=Q61058243}}''.
*Used as a location in the 2023 TV drama ''{{ill|Vivant (TV series)|Q116919744|qid=Q116919744}}'' as a contact point for the protagonists’ special unit.
